[HarnessEntry(id='continual_arc_recolor_solid_3x3_interiors_per_component_marker', kind='memory', title='Continual ARC: recolor solid 3x3 interiors per component marker', content="Task pattern (observed task-7d7db106): Grid has background 0, base color 1, and one or more marker colors (e.g. 2,3,4,6,8) embedded in the 1-shapes. Find 4-connected components of all nonzero cells; each marked component has a marker color. For each cell in a marked component, if its entire centered 3x3 neighborhood (all 9 cells, including diagonals) is nonzero, recolor that center cell to that component's marker color. Leave boundary cells and unmarked components unchanged. Marker values count as occupied when checking neighborhoods; a marker itself may be recolored to its component marker color (unchanged in value). Different disconnected components use their own marker. Demonstrated with multiple colors in 20x20/18x18 and solved 30x30 test; initial mistake was painting all qualifying interiors with one marker color instead of assigning color by 4-connected component.", path='continual_arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={'task_id': 'task-7d7db106'}, source='agent', created_at='2026-11-02T00:08:32.755816+00:00', updated_at='2026-11-02T00:08:32.755842+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='continual_arc_task_12c29693_recurring_object_recoloring_puzzle_unsolved', kind='memory', title='Continual-ARC task-12c29693: recolor the farther duplicate object', content="Task-12c29693 recurring object recoloring. Recurrent behavior: preserve grid except recolor a single non-background object to the color of a distinctive elongated L/bar component. This task was previously unsolved after 8 demo pairs; that test's failed guesses are retained below. A later fresh instance was solved correctly with one invalid-grid submission first (a row had 28 cells instead of 29), then a valid answer.

Successful fresh test (15x29, bg=5): a special color-2 marker forms a long bent line at rows0-5, c22 plus row5 c22-28. The object of color0 at rows2-5, cols16-18 (mask 3x3 rows ###/###/### then ##., 11 cells) had an identical-shape counterpart of color8 at rows0-3, cols24-26. Recolor the farther copy (color0 object) to marker color2; leave matching color8 object unchanged. This exact answer was accepted. A plausible rule is that when identical-shape objects occur in different colors, recolor the copy farther from the long L/bar marker into the marker color. Treat this as a useful hypothesis, not a universal rule: other demos had less-obvious target selection.

Demonstrations from this fresh instance (input object -> output color; background omitted):
1) bg3, a 7-cell color1 object at bottom-left (rows16-18, c5-7; shape rows XX/.XX/XXX) became color2. Long marker color2 was an L/bar near upper-right.
2) bg6, top-left irregular 14-cell color2 object became color7; marker color7 was long bent bar at lower-left.
3) bg0, 2-cell color6 domino at r4 c14-15 became color9; marker color9 was a long bent bar at top-left. There were other color6 cells/pairs, so simplistic largest-of-color does not explain every target.
4) bg3, 7-cell color0 object at rows16-18 c7-9 (shape 2/3/2) became color9; marker color9 was long bent object near top-center.
5) bg6, 3-cell color5 L at bottom-left (r17 c0-1, r18 c0) became color2; marker color2 was long L at top-left.
6) bg7, 3-cell color9 L at rows20-21 c6-7 became color1; marker color1 was large L/bar at bottom-left.
7) bg4, 2x4 color7 rectangle at rows10-13 c16-17 became color3; marker color3 was long vertical bar with horizontal top segment at bottom-right.
8) bg9, singleton color4 at r0c12 became color1; marker color1 was L/bar top-left. Another singleton color0 at r0c3 stayed unchanged; target was farther from marker.
These reinforce recoloring to a long L/bar object's color; distance and duplicate-shape relations may be important, but full selector rule remains uncertain.

Earlier test recorded on previous recurrence (11x17,bg7): main color2 L at r6 c12-16 plus r7-10 c12; color0 7-cell mask rows1-3 c7-9 = ..#/###/###; color3 L triomino r1 c13-14,r2 c14 and a separate color3 vertical pair r9-10 c6; color8 rectangle 4x2 at r5-8 c2-3, vertical trio r6-8 c10, and 7-cell shape at r8c16 and r9-10 c14-16 identical to color0 mask; color4 singleton r10c0. Attempts failed: (a) color3 L->2 plus bottom-right 8 shape->0; (b) bottom-right 8 shape->2 alone; (c) aligned color3 L->2 alone; (d) aligned color8 vertical trio->2 alone; (e) aligned bottom-right 8 shape->0 alone. Do not repeat. Those failures show matching-shape mapping is not enough unless correct copy/marker and target selection are identified.

Parsing care: all submitted grids must have consistent dimensions; initial answer here was rejected as invalid because last row had 28 rather than 29 cells. Check row lengths before submission.

Additional recurrence evidence (new 8-demo stream; selector still not fully solved):
- Demo 1: bg0; marker color9 is L/bar at lower-right. Recolored one large color2 object in upper-right (rows6-10 approx cols17-21) to 9; another small color2 pair near marker stayed unchanged.
- Demo 2: bg6; marker color9 L at lower-right. Recolored a color5 irregular object near center-right (approx rows13-15, cols12-17) to 9. Other color5 pieces stayed.
- Demo 3: bg2; marker color6 L at left around row3. Recolored irregular color3 5-cell object at rows1-2, cols7-9 to 6.
- Demo 4: bg2; marker color1 L at upper-left (vertical c6, horizontal r5). Recolored color8 horizontal 3-cell object at row5 cols11-13 to 1. There was another identical 3-cell horizontal color8 object at row3 cols1-3; the farther copy was recolored. This supports an identical-shape/farther-copy selector in at least some instances.
- Demo 5: bg8; marker color5 L at upper-right. Recolored irregular 5-cell color0 object at rows1-4, cols3-4 to 5.
- Demo 6: bg2; marker color4 L upper-left. Recolored large 11-cell color6 object (rows8-9, cols13-18) to 4.
- Demo 7: bg0; marker color8 L upper-left. Recolored color5 vertical domino at rows6-7, col24 to 8.
- Demo 8: bg4; marker color3 L upper-right (vertical c15, horizontal r4). Recolored a 3-cell L-shaped color0 object at r8c10/r9c9-10 to 3. A same-shape color9 L was near marker at r1c20/r2c19-20, and the farther copy was recolored. This further supports farther-copy for some selector cases.

Failed fresh test after 8 demos, not solved (8/8 attempts used): bg8, marker color1 is large L/bar at rows19-24, c21 plus row19 c21-28. Single-object-to-marker-color guesses all failed. Failed candidates were: (1) color0 14-cell irregular object rows14-17 cols20-23; (2) color5 4-cell L object cells (18,12),(19,11-12),(20,12); (3) color3 vertical 5-bar at rows0-4,c11; (4) color3 L triomino at (8,18),(9,18-19); (5) color5 L triomino at (7,21),(7,22),(8,21); (6) color3 horizontal domino at row0 cols1-2; (7) color0 vertical 3-bar rows5-7,c12; (8) color0 vertical domino rows4-5,c0. These failures specifically show that simple alignment-to-marker, nearest/farthest object, and guessed far-copy pairs are insufficient; don't repeat these candidate changes without new reasoning.

Selector remains unresolved: recoloring one object to distinctive L/bar marker's color is strongly consistent; identical-shape farther copy is supported by several examples and a prior accepted case, but cannot be applied indiscriminately (the current test had several plausible matching shapes, and all eight guesses failed). In future recurrence, use demos to identify which matching object class/selector is active before committing. Check exact shape/dimensions when submitting.

Confirmed selector from another solved fresh test (19x17, bg3; 8 demos): marker was the large color6 L/bar (vertical c3 rows0-5, horizontal row6 c0-3). Two identical color7 L-triominoes occurred: near marker at r0c0/r1c0-1, and far away at r12c13/r13c13-14. Recolor ONLY the farther copy (the lower-right 7 L) to marker color6; preserve the nearby identical 7 L and every other cell. First submission recoloring both copies was incorrect; the second, changing only the farther one, was correct. This strongly supports the selector: when duplicate shapes are present, recolor the copy farther from the distinctive elongated L/bar marker, not every copy. The task’s target can be a component matching another component’s shape class; choose the farther matching copy. In this test, only 3 cells changed: (12,13), (13,13), (13,14) 7→6.


Confirmed new recurrence (24x16, bg=4): marker color7 is an L/bar at rows0-6,c12 plus row6,c12-15. There are two identical 3-cell L triominoes: color8 at rows2-3, cols7-8, and color3 at rows3-4, cols14-15. Recolor ONLY the farther copy (color8 at upper-left) to marker color7; leave the near color3 copy and the unrelated large color8 object at rows15-18,c0-2 unchanged. Accepted answer confirmed. The three failed hypotheses were changing the large 8 object, changing the color3 L, or changing both small L copies. This is direct additional evidence that among identical-shape copies, recolor the one farther from the L/bar marker, converting the whole component to marker color. This reinforces the farther-duplicate selector confirmed in other solved recurrences above.


New recurrence confirmed (19x14, background 2): special marker color4 forms an L, horizontal row13 c10-13 and vertical c10 rows13-18. Two identical 6-cell objects share mask ##/##/#./#.: color8 at rows13-16,c8-9 (cells c8-9 in rows13-14, then c8 in rows15-16), and color7 at rows15-18,c12-13 (c12-13 in rows15-16, then c12 in rows17-18). Correct output recolors ONLY the color8 copy to 4; preserve the 7 copy. My first submission incorrectly recolored the 7 copy and was rejected; recoloring the 8 copy was accepted. For this selection, compare copy centers/distances to the marker, not simply closest boundary cell: the chosen 8 copy’s center is farther from marker’s center than the 7 copy’s. This is further confirmation of the farther identical-shape-copy selector (shape match + farther copy -> marker color).

Five demos from this recurrence (use as supporting evidence; target is one non-background component and output uses the prominent L/bar color): D1 background2, marker6 (large L at rows9-13 near left); upper-left color5 pattern recolored to6. D2 bg1, marker9 L at top-left; a lone color8 cell (r16,c11) changed to9. D3 bg1, marker2 L at bottom-left; color0 horizontal domino at r27,c16-17 changed to2. D4 bg2, marker8 long bent bar at bottom-left; color7 horizontal triple at r3,c19-21 changed to8. D5 bg6, marker3 L at upper-left; a color7 3-cell L at rows7-8,c24-25 changed to3. These demos alone do not reveal target selection; preserve the duplicate-shape/farther-copy hypothesis as well-supported but avoid arbitrary candidates.


Confirmed recurrence solved at zero wrong submissions (14x23, bg=8). Marker was the color5 L/bar component: horizontal run at row10 cols18-22, with vertical extension at col18 rows10-13 (8 cells total). Two identical 2x3 solid rectangles were present: color1 at rows12-13 cols5-7 and color7 at rows12-13 cols20-22. Recolor ONLY the farther copy (color1, lower-left) to marker color5; leave the nearer color7 rectangle and all other cells unchanged. Accepted output confirms same-shape farther-from-marker selector, using object/component centers (the color1 rectangle is far from the color5 marker; the color7 rectangle is close). Other components include color6 irregular 13-cell cluster, color9 vertical-ish object and separate stripe, several color3 objects; none changed. This was solved immediately, no demos required.
